business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction; SARL registration exclusively at national level via the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés - RNCS)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; company law codified in the Code de commerce; AML/CFT codified in the Code monétaire et financier)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Republic of France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (1967, as amended by the 2006 Protocol)
Agreement between France and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1984, as amended in 2013)
Convention between France and the United Kingdom on the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2008)
Convention between France and Germany for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1959, as amended; integrated into EU Arbitration Convention framework)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement - CETA (provisionally applied since 21 September 2017)
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force since 1 February 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-60 and R. 561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT obligations); Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Loi Sapin II) establishing the French UBO register; Décret n° 2017-1094 du 12 juin 2017 (UBO registration and declaration details); Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 12 février 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4th AML Directive) as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on wire transfers; INPI/RNCS UBO declaration form (Formulaire M/UBO); Tracfin implementing instruction PN-2021-01 and guide du déclarant.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted regime following CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-458/20 of 22 November 2022 invalidating general public access; access now limited to competent authorities, Tracfin, reporting/obliged entities conducting due diligence, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest as defined by implementing decree)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of each beneficial owner, manager, and shareholder occupying over 25% of capital or voting rights
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry, passport authority, or notary of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (France is a 1961 Hague Apostille Convention member; consular legalization applies only for non-member states such as Canada or certain Middle Eastern jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the French incorporation agent or avocat to sign and file incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent notarial body of the state of residence of the grantor

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing (or equivalent) of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or competent corporate registrar

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, issued within the last 3 months) for each UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, or municipal authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / judicial record extract for each manager (gérant) and each UBO holding management functions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, UBOs, and proposed managers against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU Council Decision (CFSP) 2014/145 et seq. and corresponding regulations), (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the OFAC SDN List (mandatory for any USD-rail Shopify Payments or correspondent banking transactions), (iv) the French national asset-freeze measures under Articles L. 562-1 to L. 562-19 of the Code monétaire et financier, and (v) Tracfin targeted financial sanctions notifications; Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) identification is mandatory under Article L. 561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier, including family members and known close associates; enhanced due diligence (EDD) and senior-management approval are required for any PEP identified; negative hits trigger mandatory Suspicious Activity Report (déclaration de soupçon) to Tracfin within statutory deadlines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), interfacing with the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS); supplementary due diligence searches via Infogreffe (greffe du tribunal de commerce) and the INPI trademark database (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name (dénomination sociale) must be expressed in French or in a Latin-script language; any non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters following French administrative transliteration standards; the name must be distinctive and lawful under Article L. 332-1 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle, must not create confusion with existing registered names or trademarks, and must not be contrary to public order, morality, or international/domestic protected indications.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a standalone de jure name reservation; the proposed name is examined by the RNCS/INPI during the incorporation filing review window of up to 30 days. Upon formal rejection for non-distinctiveness or conflict with a prior right, the applicant may: (i) file an immediate corrective filing via the Guichet unique with a modified distinctive token at no additional statutory filing fee; (ii) contest the rejection by filing an administrative appeal (recours administratif préalable) with the INPI within 15 days; (iii) thereafter, bring an urgent application before the presiding judge of the competent Tribunal de commerce (référé) within 1 month, and subsequently appeal to the Cour d'appel within 15 days of the first instance ruling. Third-party opposition to a conflicting name may be raised under Article L. 333-1 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle before the INPI, which stays registration until opposition is resolved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted in principle for ISIC 4791 Shopify DTC brand. Under Articles L. 123-11-2 and R. 123-139 of the Code de commerce, the siège social may lawfully be domiciled at an approved commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) holding the requisite INPI/Préfecture approval. However, the incorporation dossier must specify a genuine operational address for e-commerce fulfillment, VAT registration, and stock/inventory allocation, and the domiciliation contract must not create a sham establishment for French tax and social purposes; DGFiP and URSSAF may disregard the domiciled seat if no real staff presence, business records, or exclusive-use facility exists.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% within the first 24 months of operation. URSSAF, DGFiP (tax authorities), and customs/e-commerce enforcement units retain the right to conduct unannounced physical inspections to verify the reality of the establishment, stock, accounting records, and staff; likelihood is mitigated by the Low_Risk standard retail e-commerce classification and absence of regulated-activity licensing, but remains non-negligible given French VAT remote-sales enforcement and anti-E-commerce-fraud controls (Tracfin coordination).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of the statuts (articles of association) of the SARL, including clauses on corporate purpose, capital distribution, gérance, and transfer of shares
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French law firm (avocat) engaged by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (€200-€300 per hour; flat fee commonly €600-€1,200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Greffe fee for immatriculation (RNCS registration) of the SARL and initial RCS certificate (extrait Kbis)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI via Guichet unique

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal publication of the incorporation notice (annonce légale) in a journal d'annonces légales authorized in the siège social department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) holding official authorization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (Décret n° 2017-862; approximately €190-€220 per insertion)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) submitted as annex to the incorporation filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / RNCS (integrated into the Guichet unique filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Included in the statutory incorporation filing fee; no separate charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation (virtual office) services for the siège social for the first 12 months, including mail handling and annual renewal
Notarization and Hague Apostille bundle for 3 origin documents (passport copies, power of attorney, corporate certificate of good standing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary and competent apostille authority (e.g., Secretary of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs) of the country of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of apostilled origin documents into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator (traducteur assermenté / expert près une cour d'appel)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC/AML pre-incorporation dossier assembly, UBO identification documentation, and PEP/sanctions screening report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (flat fee per screening report)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-36 governing sociétés à responsabilité limitée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing the Trade and Companies Register; Law No. 2019-486 of 22 May 2019 requiring filings through the electronic business formalities portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Commercial Court Registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), acting through the National Business Formalities Portal operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of creation of a legal entity (formalité de création) submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, resulting in registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés and issuance of the SIREN and SIRET numbers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies; capital may be set at EUR 1 or more. For cash contributions, at least 20% must be paid upon incorporation and the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Contributions are deposited into a blocked account where applicable, and the deposit certificate is used for registration. In-kind contributions must be transferred and described in the articles; an independent contributions auditor is generally required unless all statutory exemption thresholds are satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscription of its issued shares by the founding shareholder(s) in the amounts stated in the articles of association and acknowledges payment of the required portion of the cash contributions. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full French address], effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed as gérant of the Company for an unlimited term, subject to the articles and applicable law, with authority to complete incorporation, banking, tax, employment, payment-service, and commercial registrations. RESOLVED, that the gérant may execute all documents necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate structure, activities, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders, registered-office provider, and the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SARL shareholders, capital, share allocation, business purpose, managing director, financial year, and French registered office. Verify that the business purpose accurately covers online retail, warehousing, importation, marketing, and related activities. Obtain a valid domiciliation agreement, lease, or proof of premises use.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the business purpose, address evidence, identity data, or domiciliation documentation before submission. Obtain written confirmation from the domiciliation provider where the registry questions the address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution by the shareholders; filing through the Guichet unique portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language articles containing the company name, legal form, registered office, corporate purpose, capital, share allocation, contribution terms, management rules, transfer restrictions, financial year, and duration. Sign the articles electronically or by wet signature. Notarization is not generally required for cash contributions; a notarial deed is required for certain real-estate contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend and re-execute defective articles. If an in-kind contribution is challenged, obtain or document the required contributions auditor report or apply the statutory exemption only where all conditions are met.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the capital deposit account and obtain the certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the draft articles, shareholder identities, beneficial-owner information, registered-office evidence, and source-of-funds information to the depositary. Deposit the required portion of cash capital and obtain the certificate of deposit. The blocked funds are released after registration upon presentation of the Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC questions, replace incomplete documents, or use a notarial depositary or Caisse des dépôts et consignations where a commercial bank declines onboarding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A newspaper authorized to publish legal notices in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed incorporation notice containing the company name, form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose summary, duration, managing director details, and registration information. Pay the applicable department-based fixed or regulated fee and obtain the publication certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct publication errors through a rectification notice or new notice before registry filing, depending on the materiality of the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI, with review by the competent Commercial Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the SARL creation form online, upload the signed articles, capital deposit certificate, legal notice certificate, registered-office evidence, managing director declaration, identity documents, non-conviction declaration, beneficial-owner filing, and required translations. Pay the portal and registry charges. Track the filing reference and respond electronically to registry queries.
required_dossiers: Managing director non-conviction and parentage declaration
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit the requested correction within the portal deadline, replace unreadable or inconsistent documents, pay any additional charge, and resubmit the formalité. If rejected, correct the stated defect and file again; judicial review may be considered for an unlawful registry refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration governance and operational onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI, tax administration, URSSAF, commercial bank, payment institutions, and applicable consumer or product regulators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain and archive the Kbis extract, SIREN, SIRET, and APE code. Release deposited capital, activate the corporate bank account, adopt the first management resolution, register for VAT where required, establish accounting records, and onboard Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal, logistics providers, and insurers. Implement website consumer-law, privacy, cookie, distance-selling, product-safety, packaging, and returns controls.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or payment-provider onboarding data, submit missing VAT evidence, and remediate website or product-compliance deficiencies before commencing the affected activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ordinary internet retail without manufacturing or regulated storage. The principal oversight authorities are the Directorate-General for Competition Policy, Consumer Affairs and Fraud Control (Direction générale de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes), the relevant prefecture, and the French Office for Biodiversity or other competent environmental authority where a regulated activity exists.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating licence is required for a standard DTC webstore selling compliant consumer goods. Separate authorizations may apply to regulated products, controlled goods, food, cosmetics, chemicals, alcohol, medical devices, or on-site warehousing activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion, through the competent regional environmental authority (Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale) and the relevant prefecture
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for a normal office-based online retail business with no industrial plant, material extraction, or regulated installation. A full or case-by-case environmental assessment may apply to a substantial warehouse, industrial installation classified for environmental protection (ICPE), or qualifying development project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific industrial discharge threshold applies where the company has no industrial emissions or process wastewater. The company must prevent unlawful discharge, segregate and transfer waste to authorized operators, comply with packaging extended producer responsibility obligations administered through approved eco-organizations, and manage hazardous substances and VOCs under applicable environmental and workplace rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No general civil-defense or occupational clearance is required for a remote online retail business. Any warehouse or public-access premises must comply with building, fire-safety, emergency-exit, electrical, accessibility, and occupational-health requirements. Premises open to the public may be subject to ERP fire-safety approval and periodic inspections; employers must complete the occupational-risk assessment, maintain the required DUERP, provide safe equipment and training, and arrange applicable inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), operating under the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery; taxpayer access via the professional portal impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel) with SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) local management; business formalities through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of the SARL through the Guichet Unique single-window portal, the DGFIP automatically registers the entity and issues the 9-digit SIREN (national corporate identifier), the 14-digit SIRET establishment identifier, and the French VAT intra-Community number (FR + two-digit key + 9-digit SIREN) once VAT liability attaches. A new business commencing taxable activity without prior incorporation formalities must file the 'déclaration d'existence' (form M0) with the competent tax office within 15 days of commencement. For cross-border EU e-commerce, the company must separately register through the French OSS portal (One-Stop-Shop) available on impots.gouv.fr to declare and pay VAT due in other EU member states, and must hold a French business bank account for the inward remittance traceability of export sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box election. A standard commercial SARL is by default within the scope of corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) under Article 206(1) of the CGI. Election mechanisms provided by the CGI include: (i) the pass-through election under Article 239 bis AA, allowing qualifying family-owned SARLs (all shareholders being natural persons within the same family and meeting statutory conditions) to be taxed as sociétés de personnes (shareholder-level income tax) instead of IS; and (ii) the reverse election under Article 206-3 CGI permitting partnerships to opt for IS. France implements the EU ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules (CGI Articles 205 A and following), which deny deduction benefits arising from hybrid entities or hybrid instruments; no unilateral entity-classification check-the-box override exists for French domestic-law entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French VAT, implementing the EU Common VAT Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration from the first taxable euro for a French-established SARL selling goods (no general exemption threshold for goods); the small-business 'franchise en base de TVA' exemption (CGI Article 293 B) applies while annual ex-VAT turnover from goods sales remains at or below EUR 91,900 (2024/2025 main threshold; tolerance EUR 101,000), subject to filing the annual turnover declaration and, upon breaching the tolerance, immediate registration. Cross-border EU distance sales to consumers remain French-taxable until the EUR 10,000 Union-wide distance-sales threshold is exceeded, beyond which OSS registration and destination-country VAT rates apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has enacted a mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting reform (Ordonnance 2022-1087 and 2024-2025 implementing decrees). From 1 September 2026 (large enterprises) and 1 September 2027 (all other taxable persons including this SARL), B2B domestic invoices must be issued and transmitted electronically in a structured data format (Factur-X, UBL or CII) through a certified Dematerialisation Platform (PDP) or the State-operated Chorus Pro gateway. For B2C cross-border and domestic online sales, mandatory 'e-reporting' of transaction data to the DGFIP must occur periodically (in practice on a near-real-time continuous feed), including Shopify settlement data. France does not impose Italian-style real-time fiscal stamping; compliance is instead enforced through structured data flows, the FEC (Fichier des Écritures Comptables) digital audit file, NF 525 cash-register certification, and automated VAT gap/reconciliation analytics. Failure to comply with e-invoicing/e-reporting obligations engages a EUR 15,000 per offence fine (CGI Article 1737) and up to EUR 250,000 criminal penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods sold by the French SARL to consumers or businesses outside the European Union qualify for 0% French VAT (exonération avec droit à déduction) under CGI Articles 262-I-1° and 258, provided legal title to the goods passes and the goods physically leave the EU within the statutory export period (normally within 90 days / 3 months of supply). Intra-Community supplies (B2B) to VAT-registered EU customers are 0% rated only where the customer holds a valid VIES-confirmed intra-Community VAT number and the supplier files periodic EC Sales Lists (état récupératif de clients). B2C DTC distance sales to consumers in other EU member states are zero-rated only when the OSS threshold (EUR 10,000) is exceeded via OSS registration; until then French VAT at the French rate applies. Sales to non-EU consumers via the Shopify storefront are treated as export distance sales and are eligible for zero-rating upon proper documentation. The input VAT attributable to exported goods (COGS, Shopify platform fees, logistics) is immediately creditable and refundable as a VAT credit pursuant to standard French refund procedures (monthly or quarterly SIE refund, or the annual 'remboursement de crédit de TVA').
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU – Déclaration Administrative Unique) submitted via DELTA-X with the Movement Reference Number (MRN) evidencing electronical release for export
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier proving physical transport of the goods out of the EU territory
Preuve de sortie du territoire de l'Union (validated exit proof, customs stamp or electronic exit confirmation from the customs systems)
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export sales contract issued by the SARL in the customer's name
VIES validation record of the EU customer's intra-Community VAT number and the corresponding EC Sales List (for zero-rated intra-EU B2B supplies only)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103 / proof of receipt of payment denominated in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFIP treats export zero-rating as a high-risk exposure area (fictitious exports, carousel fraud, and sham EU distance sales). The audit window for the administration is 3 years under LPF Articles L12-L16, extended to 10 years in cases of concealed or undeclared activity. Penalties for fraudulent export zero-rating include: (i) 100% major-omission penalty on the VAT amount concealed (CGI Article 1728); (ii) 80% penalty under the abuse-of-law procedure (LPF Article L64; 100% where the scheme involves non-cooperative jurisdictions or total opacity); (iii) retrospective clawback of all zero-rated input VAT credits with late-payment interest accruing at 0.80% per month, immediately enforceable via the State tax lien (hypothèque légale); (iv) criminal tax-fraud charges under CGI Article 1741 carrying up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment for the SARL's legal representative; and (v) personal joint-and-several civil liability of the manager (gérant) for penalties and restitution under CGI Article 1750 and general corporate law rules. The burden of proving physical export rests exclusively on the seller; contemporaneous customs and carrier records, FX repatriation within the 180-day rule, and complete e-reporting feeds are decisive mitigating evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, within the Eurosystem governed by the European Central Bank; banking and payment-services supervision is principally conducted by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution and, where applicable, the European Central Bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and operates within the European Union single market. The euro is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax, customs, foreign direct investment screening, and bank due-diligence controls. A French SARL may receive foreign investment, hold foreign-currency accounts where accepted by its bank, pay foreign suppliers, and remit dividends or other distributions to non-resident shareholders without a general exchange-control approval. Distributions remain subject to corporate-law requirements, distributable-profit limitations, annual accounts approval, solvency considerations, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner verification, treaty eligibility, and evidence of the underlying transaction. Transfers involving sanctioned jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, unusual payment chains, high-risk jurisdictions, or insufficient economic substance may be delayed, rejected, frozen, or reported. Interest, royalties, management fees, and related-party payments require transfer-pricing support, withholding-tax review, and documentation of services or intellectual-property rights.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or universal deadline requiring a French SARL to convert export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in euros or another permitted currency, subject to the bank account agreement, accounting requirements, tax reporting, sanctions controls, and payment-service-provider policies. The company should maintain commercial invoices, customs records, transport evidence, customer contracts, payment reconciliations, and foreign-currency accounting records. Cash movements into or out of the European Union of EUR 10,000 or more, or its equivalent, are subject to applicable customs cash-declaration rules. Foreign bank accounts and payment accounts may trigger French tax-reporting obligations, including applicable account declarations and disclosures in the annual corporate tax filing; the precise filing treatment depends on account type, holder status, and statutory exceptions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank / relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
BPCE group bank, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entity selected for the company
Crédit Mutuel group bank selected for the company

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection and operating payments, but not a universal substitute for a French bank. A regulated European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide EUR payment accounts, SEPA transfers, cards, foreign-currency collection, and merchant settlement, subject to its licence scope and safeguarding model. It may not provide ordinary bank deposits, deposit-guarantee protection, unrestricted credit, or statutory capital-deposit services unless the institution and product legally support those functions. Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe onboarding remains separate from corporate-bank onboarding and requires consistent legal-name, tax, beneficial-owner, website, product, refund, and settlement information. Offshore digital EMIs without an applicable European passport, French authorisation, or lawful cross-border service basis present elevated account-closure, safeguarding, data, sanctions, and payment-finality risks. The company should maintain a regulated French or EEA primary bank account and use fintech accounts as controlled secondary rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that every director physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted for a French SARL where the bank accepts electronic identification and documentary verification. Banks may nevertheless require a video interview, certified identity documents, specimen signatures, a French registered-office verification, a live call with the manager or beneficial owner, or an in-person meeting for non-resident directors, complex ownership, foreign shareholders, high transaction volumes, unusual jurisdictions, or failed electronic verification. Capital-deposit account procedures may require documents issued by the formation professional, notarial office, or legal representative and may be subject to bank-specific signing formalities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent SARL formation records, including missing registration extract, articles of association, registered-office evidence, tax identifier, or appointment documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent extrait Kbis or equivalent registration evidence, executed articles of association, certificate of incorporation or registration, SIREN and SIRET details, proof of registered office, beneficial-owner filing, manager appointment, board or shareholder authority, and current corporate structure chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee ownership, layered foreign holding companies, or inability to identify natural-person controllers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ownership chart to each natural person, passports and address evidence for each beneficial owner and authorised signatory, shareholder register, foreign corporate extracts, trust or foundation documents where relevant, control analysis, and signed beneficial-owner certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or directors, residence in a high-risk jurisdiction, or cross-border ownership inconsistent with the stated French retail activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Residence evidence, tax-residence information, source-of-wealth statement, source-of-funds evidence, shareholder investment agreement, bank statements, audited accounts where available, group structure explanation, and written business rationale for the French operating entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: DTC e-commerce model with insufficient website transparency, restricted products, intellectual-property uncertainty, dropshipping indicators, or mismatch between website content and declared business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live website and Shopify store access, product catalogue, supplier contracts, invoices, brand and trademark evidence, fulfilment and logistics contracts, terms and conditions, privacy and cookie notices, returns and refund policy, consumer-law disclosures, product-safety evidence, and payment-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payment activity inconsistent with the low-risk profile, including high-volume card receipts, rapid pass-through payments, multiple unrelated counterparties, excessive refunds, or unexplained cash flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month transaction forecast, monthly volume and average-ticket assumptions, customer geography, chargeback and refund controls, payment-provider statements, reconciliations, management accounts, cash-flow forecast, settlement-cycle explanation, and documented treasury approval controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained third-party payments, personal-account usage, shareholder loans without documentation, or transfers between the SARL and related parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements, shareholder-loan agreements, invoices, service descriptions, transfer-pricing support, payment approval matrix, related-party register, bank reconciliations, and evidence that operating funds are segregated from personal funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, corruption, or restricted-country exposure involving an owner, customer, supplier, logistics provider, or payment intermediary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results, enhanced due-diligence questionnaire, beneficial-owner verification, counterparties' registration records, sanctions representations, geographic-risk policy, transaction-monitoring controls, escalation records, and evidence of refusal or blocking procedures for prohibited transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of the initial capital contribution or subsequent shareholder funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreement, capital contribution schedule, originating bank statements, audited financial statements or tax returns of the funding shareholder, sale or dividend documentation where relevant, loan agreement, and traceable transfer from an account held in the funder's own name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax, customs, VAT, or consumer-compliance inconsistency, particularly for imported goods and sales to EU consumers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: VAT registration or applicability analysis, OSS/IOSS evidence where relevant, customs registrations, EORI number, import records, tariff classification, delivery terms, tax filings, inventory records, and written explanation of customer-location and tax-collection controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of an offshore EMI, virtual-asset service, anonymous payment instrument, or unregulated payment intermediary as a principal treasury account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licence and regulatory-register extract, safeguarding terms, account ownership proof, transaction statements, source-of-funds trail, compliance policy, rationale for use, and confirmation that regulated French or EEA banking remains the primary account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity through a regulated bank account held in the subscriber's legal name into the French SARL capital-deposit account or operational account, using a clear payment reference such as share capital subscription or shareholder loan, as legally applicable. Before transfer, provide the bank with the subscription agreement, draft or executed articles, shareholder identity and beneficial-owner evidence, source-of-funds documents, corporate resolutions, and expected amount and currency. The bank should record the originator, beneficiary, purpose, intermediary banks, and ultimate source of funds. For a capital increase, obtain the required corporate approvals, deposit certificate, updated registration filing, and post-closing capital records. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated third parties, cash, privacy-enhancing instruments, or opaque multi-hop structures. SEPA Credit Transfer is appropriate for EUR transfers within the SEPA area; SWIFT cross-border transfer is appropriate for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. Use accurate ISO 20022 payment data and retain MT103 or equivalent payment confirmation where issued. Payment-purpose wording must be truthful and must not be used to evade sanctions, reporting, tax, or bank controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible EUR suppliers within SEPA, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. Use SWIFT customer credit transfer, historically evidenced by MT103 and increasingly processed through ISO 20022 pacs.008 messaging, for non-SEPA suppliers and foreign currencies. For higher-value or documentary transactions, use a commercial letter of credit subject to UCP 600, with electronic presentation only where the applicable rules and bank agree; use documentary collections under URC 522 where suitable. Match each payment to purchase orders, commercial invoices, customs and shipping documents, supplier master data, and proof of delivery. The bank may request the transaction purpose, HS classification, end-use, country of origin, Incoterms, sanctions screening, and beneficial-owner information. Separate supplier payments, tax payments, payroll, refunds, merchant settlements, and shareholder distributions in the treasury ledger. Conduct sanctions screening before release and maintain dual approval, beneficiary-change call-back, payment limits, and bank-reconciliation controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forward contracts with an authorised bank or regulated investment firm, supported by documented forecast exposures and subject to MiFID II appropriateness, suitability, product-governance, and client-classification requirements where applicable.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to legal availability, counterparty policy, market documentation, sanctions screening, and appropriate ISDA or bank master-agreement terms.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing recurring funding or settlement exposures, subject to counterparty credit limits, valuation, collateral, and applicable European Market Infrastructure Regulation obligations.
Foreign-exchange spot transactions for operational conversion of collected revenues and supplier-payment requirements.

Currency options, including purchased vanilla options or approved option structures, only where the SARL understands premium, volatility, collateral, liquidity, and loss risks and the regulated counterparty has approved the product.
Natural hedging through matching currency receipts and payments, currency-denominated supplier contracts, settlement-account segmentation, and documented exposure netting.

Hedging must relate to genuine commercial or financing exposures, be approved under a written treasury policy, be recorded under applicable French GAAP or IFRS accounting rules, and not constitute unauthorised investment activity or speculative dealing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in a court injunction, a civil fine of approximately EUR 1,500, increased to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance, and potential director liability. France has no automatic annual administrative strike-off solely for late accounts filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end, subject to electronic filing rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, increased penalties for deliberate or repeated non-compliance, and tax-audit exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approval record and management report, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at the registered office; approval resolutions are available to the Commercial Court Registry upon filing requirements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the annual accounts within six months after the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the approval meeting may create manager liability, permit judicial compulsion, and impair timely statutory accounts filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner information review and amendment filing, if required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French one-stop business formalities portal and the competent Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual beneficial-owner filing is required. Changes to beneficial-owner information must generally be reported within 30 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or maintain accurate beneficial-owner information may result in judicial injunctions, criminal penalties, restrictions on access to certain corporate services, and liability for the legal representative.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the relevant reporting date: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover excluding VAT, and 50 average employees. Appointment may also be required in certain controlled-group structures or voluntarily by shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (Autorité des normes comptables). IFRS is not generally mandatory for an individual SARL's statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation. The SARL should conduct an annual internal verification of ownership and control data, update its beneficial-owner filing after any change, and report changes generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be documented and the register of shareholders updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and share transfers
Register of shareholders' decisions and minutes
Accounting books and supporting accounting documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_government_renewal_fees: Approximately USD 49 for annual accounts filing; no general annual franchise or company-renewal fee applies to a French SARL.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-2,500 per year for a commercial registered-office service, depending on location and mail-handling services. France generally does not require a separate statutory registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,200-9,000 for a small SARL, depending on transaction volume, group structure, inventory, payroll, and audit complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard rate; 15% reduced rate on first €42,000 of taxable profit for companies with turnover < €10 million
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate for small businesses; Research Tax Credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses; Innovation Tax Credit (CIT) for SMEs; no statutory tax holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (with annexes 2050-2059) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr (professional online filing)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly advance payments on March 15, June 15, Sept 15, Dec 15)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending December 31, online filing due by May 3; for other fiscal year ends, within 3 months of year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must file via a fiscal representative if no permanent establishment; report French-source income only
Indicate prior-year losses available for offset; subject to annual cap of €1 million plus 50% of excess profit
Claim eligible credits (e.g., CIR) with supporting documentation; non-residents may claim if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax paid on foreign income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign withholding taxes and claim treaty relief if applicable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of tax due, plus 0.20% monthly interest; additional 40% penalty for intentional omission; criminal sanctions for fraud

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% standard rate; reduced to 15% (portfolio) or 5% (substantial shareholding ≥10%) under US-France treaty; other treaties vary
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form 5000 (or equivalent) to the French tax authority; obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from home country; apply for reduced rate at payment or claim refund within 5 years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33%, reduced to 15% or 0% under treaties; Interest: statutory 30%, generally exempt under treaties if not from tax haven

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full documentation required if French entity turnover ≥ €50 million or group turnover ≥ €400 million; simplified documentation for SMEs below thresholds
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) and substance requirements for treaty benefits; ESR not applicable (non-offshore jurisdiction), but substance is required to avoid abuse of law

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false deductions, or concealment of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 40% of understated tax (80% for abuse of law); criminal fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for tax debts if found to have participated in fraud; travel bans and asset freezes possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lack of economic substance, artificial arrangements to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions; denial of treaty benefits; penalty of 80% of tax avoided; potential criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for unpaid taxes and penalties; possible criminal sanctions including imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement anti-money laundering controls, suspicious transaction reporting, or KYC procedures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €5 million or 5% of turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for non-compliance; may face criminal charges and disqualification from management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length prices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income; penalty of 5% of adjusted amount (up to 40% for serious non-compliance); interest on underpayment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; potential criminal liability for fraud
